title: The Normative Inversion of EU law
description: This paper argues that the European Union has undergone a silent constitutional transformation, wherein the formal architecture of conferral and subsidiarity has been inverted through procedural formalism, legal semantics, and strategic misapplication of internal market competences. Using the proposed CSA Regulation, MiCA, DSA, and AI Act as case studies, it demonstrates how Article 114 TFEU is systematically exploited to enact criminal-law-adjacent measures without respecting the substantive safeguards enshrined in Articles 82 and 83 TFEU. By reframing criminal enforcement as market harmonization, the EU institutions, particularly the Commission, expand regulatory power beyond the Treaties’ intended scope. This regulatory drift threatens both the structural integrity of the EU legal order and the constitutional identity of Member States, particularly in systems like Germany’s, where legality is defined substantively. The result is a post-legal governance model that performs legality while hollowing out its constraints—a phenomenon that must be addressed to preserve the rule of law in the EU
